Equal Treatment Bench Book – July 2024 (February 2026 update) 70
• Avoiding making too many orders/giving too many instructions at once.
• Avoiding setting too many different dates for various directions to be complied with.
• Extending time limits for taking action.
• Holding preliminary hearings to resolve case preparation as opposed to written
communications or telephone case management.
• Allowing longer for case management/preliminary hearings.
• Making necessary adjustments to any case management/preliminary hearings (room
layout/interpreter etc). Many of the adjustments which would also be needed at a full
hearing/trial may be necessary at preliminary hearings. This should not be overlooked for
preliminary hearings.
• Not floating case management preliminary hearings. If several are listed together, taking
the disabled person’s preliminary/case management hearing first.
• Holding all or part of the hearing by telephone or video.
• Expediting the final hearing date (if possible).
